title: channel_recent pagination (cursor for deep history)

story.as_a: coding agent (or dashboard) reviewing a repo's coordination history
story.i_want_to: page back through channel posts beyond the most recent 100
story.so_that: I can review the full 30-day window of activity, not just the newest page

rationale: v1 caps channel_recent at 100 recency-only — fine for 'what happened lately' but not for reviewing history or backing the dashboard (US-40.6). A stable cursor over (inserted_at, id) enables deep reads without offset drift as new posts arrive.

background.includes: Keyset/cursor pagination over (inserted_at DESC, id), consistent with any existing loopctl cursor convention.

acceptance_criteria.description: channel_recent accepts an optional cursor encoded/decoded via the existing Loopctl.KeysetCursor (integrity-protected, tenant-bound, namespaced — returns {:error, :invalid} on tamper/cross-tenant); the response meta returns next_cursor when more rows exist and null when exhausted, using the established %{data, has_more, next_cursor} shape.
Keyset pagination is stable under concurrent inserts (no skipped/duplicated rows across pages), unlike offset. Still filters expires_at > now() and the tenant/project scope.
Backward compatible: without a cursor, behavior is exactly US-39.3 (newest page, limit<=100).

test_cases.name: cursor pages the full set without gaps
steps: page with limit=100 following next_cursor to exhaustion
expected_results: all 250 seen exactly once; final next_cursor null

test_cases.name: insert during paging doesn't drift
preconditions: page 1 fetched, then a new post inserted
expected_results: no row from page 1 reappears; no row skipped

technical_notes: Keyset: WHERE (inserted_at, id) < (cursor_inserted_at, cursor_id) ORDER BY inserted_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT n.
Use Loopctl.KeysetCursor (lib/loopctl/keyset_cursor.ex) to encode/decode — do NOT roll base64-of-tuple (tamperable, no tenant binding = a security regression vs the existing helper).

Match the established meta shape %{data, has_more, next_cursor} (change_controller.ex:122-127, audit.ex:202-215). Note the repo has a mixed convention (article_controller uses offset); keyset is the right choice here.
